title: Easel: posting, gifts, leaning and joining in the engine; the sweep
why: Open 0, New 1, Miss 1, Importance 1, Reach 2 = 5, haiku high on the ladder. Every rule, field, action, formula and tie-break is in the spec, adapted from the levy and the market's trade. It runs every turn. Off the ladder up to sonnet medium: it adds a trader to the clearing, a step, two actions, a Config flag and a sweep mode across civs, markets, clans, world, the CLI and cross-build.mjs, which must stay in step with lead_orders. I expect Sonnet to land it in one attempt with replay and cross-build green and no change of form, where Haiku would likely miss a mirror or a serde default and need a second attempt. The retro can check that. Part and score agree: an easel well under 12.

title: Easel: leaning clans, the keep and gift controls, and the feed on the page
why: Open 2, New 1, Miss 1, Importance 0, Reach 1 = 5: haiku high. Plain JS panels in select.js's patterns, view fields from existing data, check.mjs as the test it extends, and part of it judged by eye from two screenshots. This is the piece's Haiku step. Part and score agree.

title: Canvas: is joining a lever worth pulling?
why: Open 4, New 1, Miss 1, Importance 1, Reach 2 = 9: opus low for a canvas. It searches for the numbers, and maybe a rule's form, that make gifts and keep a lever worth pulling against the AI. It's judged by the sweep against its control and a led civ, and by playing the panel. It may change the easel. A canvas at 9 holds the hard part.

title: Review the piece
why: Open 2, New 1, Miss 3, Importance 1, Reach 2 = 9: by coin, sonnet high. It checks founding.md and the piece's Decided lines against the engine, judges the canvas's changes of form, copies sweep.md's answer into the PR, and plays a led civ raising its gift until a clan joins.
